text:
maria: FYI — noticed a weird SLO burn spike for inference-serving yesterday around 03:40 UTC. The per-region dashboard shows identical high burn for us-west and eu-west at the same time :thinking:
alex: I saw that too. Dashboard rollup looks suspicious — I think we're double-counting the same requests across region labels.
sam: How are we tagging region on our envoy/nginx metrics today? I thought we used cluster->region mapping.
alex: We do, but some older clusters still export region=unknown and we also have cluster_id and az labels. Our promql rollup was doing sum(rate(...)) without grouping by region label explicitly, so duplicates slip through when labels differ.
katie: If that's true we should change the SLI recording rule to pre-aggregate by (slo, region) and then sum for global. Quick patch suggestion:
```
# recording rule
- record: sli:latency_p99:region
  expr: sum by (slo_id, region) (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, slo_id, region)))
```
Then global: sum without double-counting: sum(sli:latency_p99:region)
maria: Nice. That would stop label combinatorics from inflating the global numbers. Could we also normalise unknown->region tag via relabelling on scrape configs?
alex: Yes — relabel to set region="unknown" -> drop cluster-level duplicates, or better set cluster->region map in prometheus relabel_configs for kube_sd.
sam: We also need to decide what to do with historical error budget numbers — last 24h is currently inflated.
katie: Two options: 1) backfill corrected rollups from archived raw metrics and recompute errorbudget, or 2) annotate the SLOs and reset the burn window after fix to avoid retroactive changes.
maria: Backfill preferred for accuracy but it's heavier. Are archived metrics in our long-term storage usable? We have 90d in Cortex.
alex: We can run a one-off job that queries Cortex raw series and writes recording-rule-style results to a temporary metric name, then swap. I can spike that tonight. ETA a few hours.
deploy-bot: deploy request: new recording rule sli:latency_p99:region added to prometheus-rules (PR #3421). CI passed.
oncall-bot: alert: SLO-burn-global firing during incident window — annotated 1795502000..1795504200 UTC.
sam: While we're touching alerts, let's make the burn-rate alert use a 15m window for reduce chatter (was 5m), and split alerts per-region so ops can page the right oncall.
katie: Agreed. Also update Grafana panels: show stacked per-region burn + a separate single global rollup line. Add a note on hover explaining the rollup method.
maria: One more thing — cost alignment. Add 'billing_region' label via cluster tagging so finance dashboards and SLOs can align for cost vs outages.
alex: I'll add relabel and a short migration doc. Also adding a check in the oncall runbook:
```
1) check: PromQL -> sum by(region) (increase in slo_errors[15m])
2) if equal spikes across regions -> look for relabel/cluster duplicate
3) if prometheus duplication confirmed -> run fix PR and annotate SLOs
```
katie: Nice. Can we also add a Grafana annotation when we flip the recording rules so historic queries know about the change?
maria: Yes, create a dashboard annotation and flag the SLO page. OK team — action items: alex spike backfill, katie update dashboards & alerts, sam validate relabels on staging, maria coordinate SLO annotations + finance tag. I'll own the postmortem doc if the backfill changes error budget materially.
alex: On it. Will post PR link and runbook edits here when ready. :thumbsup:
katie: Thanks — tagging @oncall for visibility when we change alerts.
oncall-bot: ack — scheduled maintenance window requested for recording-rule update 1795509000..1795512600 UTC.
__notes: This Slack thread documents an eng-sre discussion about fix for double-counting in SLO rollups across regions, recording-rule changes, backfill vs annotate decision, alert tuning, Grafana updates, and cost tagging. Messages are short and in chronological order as a single continuous string per agents.md instructions.
